title: Find the CO₂ in the air
hook: You breathe out carbon dioxide all day. How much of the air around you is it?

knows: that air is a mixture of gases
that a drop holds about 10^21 molecules (molecules-in-one-drop)
doesNotKnow: what a share of a few parts per million looks like
that a tiny share can still be an enormous count

misconception: Carbon dioxide is a sizeable part of air (several per cent or more), and 'a few parts per million' means 'almost none there'.
objective: The learner can say that only about 4 in 10,000 molecules of dry air are CO2 (about 420 ppm, 0.042%), and that this tiny share is still about 5 x 10^18 molecules in one breath.

claims.text: Dry air is about 78.08% nitrogen, 20.95% oxygen and 0.93% argon by volume (molecule count): of 10,000 molecules, 7,808 nitrogen, 2,095 oxygen and 93 argon (stage legend; reveal: 'Of your 10,000 dots, 7,808 were nitrogen, 2,095 oxygen, 93 argon').
claims.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Composition of dry air' / U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (N2 78.084%, O2 20.946%, Ar 0.934%). Per 10,000: 7,808.4, 2,094.6, 93.4, rounded. Brief claim 1.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Opened the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 sea-level volume fractions as transcribed in PyPI ussa1976 0.3.4 (constants.py, F: N2 0.78084, O2 0.209476, Ar 0.00934; cites NASA-TM-X-74335). Per 10,000: 7,808.4, 2,094.8, 93.4, rounded to 7,808, 2,095, 93. Cross-check: OpenStax Astronomy 2e 'The Massive Atmosphere of Venus' (m59840) table, Earth N2 78.1%, Ar 0.93%, O2 21.0%; OpenStax Chemistry 2e 9.1 (m68750) 78.1% N2, 21.0% O2. The CRC table was not opened.

claims.text: Carbon dioxide was about 425 parts per million of the atmosphere in 2025, 0.043%, about 4 of every 10,000 molecules (question answer; stage legend 'CO₂ 4'; reveal: 'only 4 carbon dioxide: about 425 parts per million in 2025, or 0.043%').
claims.source: NOAA GML global marine-surface annual mean CO2, 2025: 425.62 ppm (data/co2-annmean-gl.csv in the datasets/co2-ppm mirror on GitHub, sourced from NOAA ESRL; opened by the fact-checker in pass 38). 425 ppm = 4.25 per 10,000 = 0.0425%, shown as 0.043%; 4 of 10,000 rounded. | Before the 2026-10-15 rewording: WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin No. 20 (October 2024): global mean 420.0 ppm for 2023; cross-check NOAA GML or Scripps Mauna Loa records. 420 ppm = 4.2 per 10,000 = 0.042%. Brief claim 2.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Opened NOAA GML global marine-surface annual means via the datasets/co2-ppm mirror on GitHub (data/co2-annmean-gl.csv, ODC-PDDL, sourced from NOAA ESRL): 2023 419.35 ppm, 2024 422.79, 2025 425.62; Mauna Loa 2023 421.08. 'About 420 ppm, 0.042%, about 4 of 10,000' holds for the cited 2023 value, and 4 of 10,000 still holds today (monthly global mean mid-2026 about 428). WMO Bulletin No. 20 itself was not opened. Non-blocking: the figure rises about 2.5 ppm a year and the stage gives no year; consider 'about 420 ppm (2023)' or update to about 425 (2025 global mean). cm-chemistry's call. | Reset to unverified by demo-builder (2026-10-15): W-867 optional wording: the CO2 figure now has a year: 'about 425 parts per million in 2025, or 0.043%' (was 'about 420 ..., or 0.042%', no year). | FC pass 42 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Opened datasets/co2-ppm data/co2-annmean-gl.csv (raw.githubusercontent.com, NOAA GML global marine-surface annual mean) this pass: 2025 425.62 ppm (2024 422.79). 'About 425 parts per million in 2025' holds. 425.62 ppm = 0.042562%, shown as 0.043%. Per 10,000 it is 4.26, shown as 4 (legend 'CO₂ 4'; Demo.tsx comment 7,808 + 2,095 + 93 + 4 = 10,000).

claims.text: The grid's 7,808 + 2,095 + 93 + 4 = 10,000 rounds each share and leaves out gases under 1 per 10,000 (neon, helium, methane, krypton, hydrogen and others, about 27 ppm in total).
claims.source: Node arithmetic (demo-builder 2026-10-14) from c1 and c2. Not stated to the learner; disclosed here. Brief claim 3.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Node: 7,808 + 2,095 + 93 + 4 = 10,000. The left-out gases in USSA 1976 (ussa1976 0.3.4 constants.py): Ne 18.18 + He 5.24 + Kr 1.14 + Xe 0.087 + CH4 2 + H2 0.5 = 27.15 ppm, 'about 27 ppm' and 0.27 per 10,000, under one dot. Not shown to learners.

claims.text: One breath of about 0.5 L of air at 25 °C and 1 atm holds about 5 x 10^18 CO2 molecules (stage: 'One breath, about 0.5 L: about 5 × 10¹⁸ CO₂ molecules'; reveal).
claims.source: n = PV/RT = 101,325 Pa x 0.0005 m^3 / (8.314 x 298.15) = 0.0204 mol; x 6.02214076e23 x 425e-6 = 5.23e18 (node; Demo.tsx BREATH_CO2). Tidal volume about 0.5 L at rest: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e 'The Process of Breathing' (opened by the fact-checker in pass 38); Guyton & Hall. Brief claim 4. | Before the 2026-10-15 rewording: n = PV/RT = 101,325 Pa x 0.0005 m^3 / (8.314 x 298.15) = 0.0204 mol; x 6.02214076e23 x 420e-6 = 5.2e18 (node). Tidal volume about 0.5 L at rest: Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, pulmonary ventilation. Brief claim 4.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Node, my own constants (R = 8.314462618): n = 101,325 x 0.0005 / (R x 298.15) = 0.02044 mol; x 6.02214076e23 x 420e-6 = 5.17e18, stage shows '5 × 10¹⁸' (toFixed(0) of 5.17); at 428 ppm 5.27e18, still 5. My own constants (R = 8.314462618): n = 101,325 × 0.0005 / (R × 298.15) = 0.020437 mol; × 6.02214076e23 × 425e-6 = 5.23e18 (5.24e18 at 425.62 ppm). The stage shows (BREATH_CO2/1e18).toFixed(0) = '5 × 10¹⁸'. Tidal volume: I opened OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e m46549 'The Process of Breathing' (raw.githubusercontent.com, openstax/osbooks-anatomy-physiology) this pass: 'Tidal volume (TV) is the amount of air that normally enters the lungs during quiet breathing, which is about 500 milliliters'.

claims.text: A part per million is a share, not an amount; a tiny share of a huge crowd is still a huge number, which is why trace gases are counted in ppm (reveal).
claims.source: Definition: 1 ppm = 1 part in 10^6 by count (mole fraction, for gases), e.g. IUPAC Gold Book on 'parts per million'; the 'huge number' follows from c4.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Definition opened in OpenStax Chemistry 2e section 3.4 'Other Units for Solution Concentrations' (m68704): ppm, 'like percentage (part per hundred)', a share. For gases the NOAA data description (datasets/co2-ppm README) defines ppm as molecules of CO2 over all molecules in dry air. The 'huge number' follows from c4 (verified). IUPAC Gold Book not opened.

claims.text: The dot positions are a seeded layout, not a sample of real air (mulberry32, seed 42; seed picked so the four CO2 rings sit apart and away from the edge, which does not change any count).
claims.source: The lesson (Demo.tsx layout()). Brief claim 5; pattern disclose-chosen-seeds.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Convention checked against the code: re-ran the mulberry32 seed 42 Fisher-Yates shuffle in node (own copy): CO2 cells (39,81), (27,45), (83,89), (38,64), closest pair 17 cells apart, none at the edge. Counts are assigned from GASES, not from the seed, so no count depends on the seed.

recall.question: A gas makes up 2 parts per million of the air. In one litre of air, is there a lot of it or almost none?
options: Almost none: 2 ppm rounds to zero
A lot: still about 5 x 10^16 molecules
recall.why: Parts per million is a share. A litre of air holds about 2.5 x 10^22 molecules, so 2 per million of them is still about 5 x 10^16 molecules.
